title: Delete provably empty large-component launch for bounded problems
evidence: The existing cooperative kernel immediately publishes empty status and returns when largeCount is zero. Complete node count<=1024 proves no large component can exist. The existing final merge can own this publication and readiness check.
proposed_mechanism: When the complete authored node count is at most the unchanged1024-node small-component limit, omit the empty cooperative launch and its occupancy query. Existing final merge publishes the same ready/error/empty status before merging small components. Larger worlds retain the original path. No device count readback, conditional graph or extra kernel.
affected_scenarios: small structural cold/warm and flying/isolated cases
city and large-connected cases as unchanged-routing controls
estimated_application_ms_saved: 0 to0.03ms small-structure tick, near zero city. This is a bounded deletion pilot, not the old0–1ms whole-city prediction.
confidence: High cardinality proof and exact status semantics; low measurable runtime benefit.
experiment_cost: Two private fragments, existing error/cap/mixed-size/free/anchored numerical and asynchronous physical gates, light before full retention.
supporting_measurements: Exact physical/error/cap semantics, one fewer empty launch, lower full steps or qualified neutral simplification. The defined empty merge supports a later separately proven immutable connectivity bound for larger all-small assets.
refuting_measurements: Any readiness or convergence-cap masking, changed physical results, or material overhead/regression.
scope: Independent compatible baseline. No earlier candidate composition or completed-experiment credit. Reuse identical control artifacts; run fresh matched timings.
